sources.title: Introducing Claude Opus 4.6
sources.evidence: February 5, 2026 announcement names Claude Opus 4.6 and API ID claude-opus-4-6; introduces adaptive thinking and 1M-token context, and describes coding, agentic and knowledge-work capabilities. Reopened 2026-10-27: launch announcement and benchmark comparison supply no nominal total or active parameter count; predecessor language does not identify a sized base model.

sources.title: Claude Opus 4.6 - Claude Platform Docs
sources.evidence: Exact model page lists February 5, 2026 release, 1M-token context, adaptive thinking, text/image input and text output, and claude-opus-4-6 ID. Reopened 2026-10-27: the current-lineup comparison table covers context, output, price, thinking, effort and cutoff, with no total or activated-parameter column; specifications contain neither count.

sources.title: Verbalizable Representations Form a Global Workspace in Language Models
sources.evidence: Methods describes Transformer residual-stream layers and Jacobian-lens analysis. The paper explicitly includes Opus 4.6 ablation experiments in the experiential-report subsection (#ws-experience) and alignment examples in section 5.3; section 5.4 calls the preceding cases production models. Pre-release audit origin is distinguished from artificially trained model organisms.

sources.title: GLM-5.3 and the spread of advanced cyber capabilities
sources.evidence: States generally that Claude weights are not publicly released or customizable. Used only for weight-distribution status, not architecture or parameter counts.

sources.title: Commercial Terms of Service
sources.evidence: Commercial API service terms reserve intellectual-property rights except the rights expressly granted; supports proprietary service classification alongside the explicit nonpublic-weight policy.

sources.title: PDF support
sources.evidence: All active models support PDF processing; the page specifically discusses Opus 4.6 and earlier on Bedrock and explains PDF text/image processing.

sources.title: Tool use with Claude
sources.evidence: Defines function calling and explicitly lists Claude Opus 4.6 tool-choice modes and tool-use system-prompt overhead.

sources.title: Claude Opus 4.6 System Card
sources.evidence: Fresh official PDF retrieved 2026-10-27T10:18:49Z and independently searched in full. Section 1.1.1 describes pretraining followed by post-training/fine-tuning without a nominal size or a separately sized named base. Section 6.4.2 starts an experiment from the Opus 4.6 base model, whose size is also unstated; its Sonnet 4-based paraphraser is an experimental auxiliary, not Opus 4.6 lineage. No total or active parameter count found; effort controls, crosscoder features and oracle activations do not supply one.

sources.title: Claude Opus 5.5 System Card
sources.evidence: Fresh official PDF retrieved 2026-10-27T10:11:48Z and independently searched for parameter counts and Opus 4.6 comparisons. Its AECI discussion compares capabilities through Opus 4.6, and its tables report benchmark performance; no nominal total or active count for Opus 4.6 was found.

sources.title: Models overview
sources.evidence: Explicitly states that Claude Opus 4.5 and Claude Opus 4.6 report the opus model line in the Models API.

sources.title: Claude Opus 4.7 System Card
sources.evidence: Fresh official PDF retrieved 2026-10-27T10:18:49Z. Section 8.1 (pages 191 onward) directly compares Opus 4.6 and Opus 4.7 using benchmark scores, without total or active parameter columns. Full-text parameter and numeric-count searches found neither count for Opus 4.6.

sources.title: Claude Opus 4.8 System Card
sources.evidence: Fresh official PDF retrieved 2026-10-27T10:18:50Z. Searched full text for nominal and active counts and inspected its Opus 4.6 comparison references; no parameter specification for Opus 4.6 found. Activated interpretability features are not activated model parameter counts.

sources.title: Claude Opus 5 System Card
sources.evidence: Fresh official PDF retrieved 2026-10-27T10:18:51Z. Full-text count and Opus 4.6 searches found evaluation references, model-grader use and effort controls, with no total or active count for Opus 4.6.

sources.title: Claude Sonnet 5.5 System Card
sources.evidence: Fresh official PDF retrieved 2026-10-27T10:11:47Z. Independently searched later comparison material for total, active and activated parameter counts; no nominal count for Opus 4.6 found. Parameter references concern effort controls.

sources.title: Claude Haiku 5.5 System Card
sources.evidence: Fresh official PDF retrieved 2026-10-27T10:11:48Z. Independently searched later comparison material for total, active and activated parameter counts; no nominal count for Opus 4.6 found. Parameter references concern effort controls.

sources.title: Anthropic Transparency Hub — Claude Opus 4.6 summary
sources.evidence: Reopened 2026-10-27. Exact-model summary describes pretraining and RLHF/RLAIF, hardware and modalities but gives no parameter count or explicit relationship to a separately sized base model.

sources.title: Estimating the Size of Claude Opus 4.5/4.6
sources.evidence: Resolved numerical lead, not specification evidence: the author estimates 93–105B active at FP8 or 127–154B with mixed FP8/FP4 from assumed effective bandwidth and observed throughput. Total estimates of approximately 1–3T depend on assumed routing/sparsity borrowed from other models. The article states Anthropic has not released size details; no developer disclosure or named-base lineage supports these estimates.

sources.title: The Memo — Special edition — Claude Opus 4.6
sources.evidence: Resolved 5T numerical lead: the author explicitly presents it as a personal estimate based on pricing, comparison models, inferred TPU supply and demand while saying model details are confidential. It is not an Anthropic nominal count.

sources.title: Claude Opus 4.6 — Research Implementation
sources.evidence: Resolved 2T total / 330B active numerical lead: the repository explicitly calls itself a speculative educational implementation, says all architecture details are inferred, and includes no actual Claude weights. Its hypothetical configuration does not establish production model size.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 review of launch, exact specifications/card, transparency summary and later first-party comparisons found no published nominal total or explicit lineage from a separately sized base. Opus 4.6 base in the scratchpad experiment has no disclosed size; predecessor/upgrade wording alone cannot establish one. Resolved 1–3T throughput-derived, 5T pricing/supply-derived and 2T hypothetical-implementation leads as estimates, not developer specifications. Null reflects absent nominal evidence, not a requirement for an exact tensor census.

active_parameters_b.note: Checked active count independently, including the current-lineup specifications table and later official cards through the Claude 5.5 family. No activated-parameter column or nominal per-token count for Opus 4.6 was found. The 93–105B/127–154B lead depends on unconfirmed serving precision and bandwidth; the 330B lead belongs to a speculative educational implementation. Effort controls and interpretability activations are not parameter counts; no dense-equals-total inference is made.

architecture.note: Exact Opus 4.6 experiments use the Transformer residual-stream/Jacobian-lens framework. Section 5.3 is from pre-release audits, while section 5.4 explicitly calls those production models; the separate experiential-report subsection also names Opus 4.6 experiments. Supports transformer only, not dense/MoE subtype or layer count (displayed layer indices are normalized).

patch.notes: Transformer architecture is supported by exact-model interpretability experiments. Anthropic has not disclosed nominal total or active parameter counts in reviewed specifications and cards; published third-party size estimates are unverified. Dense/MoE subtype remains undisclosed. PDF input denotes document processing through text and vision.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retains total and active counts as undisclosed after fresh launch/specification/card review, later official comparison checks through Claude 5.5, and resolution of numeric and named-base leads. The 1–3T, 5T, 2T and associated active-count claims are assumption-based estimates or hypothetical implementations, not developer specifications. Prior non-parameter assessments are preserved, including transformer architecture, proprietary classification, February 5 release, 1M context and documented capabilities.
